codes.label: Writes boilerplate and repetitive code
codes.definition: The assistant produces routine, repetitive code such as boilerplate, getters, setters and config files.
codes.include: Answers naming boilerplate or repetitive code as something it writes well.

anchor_quotes.quote: Quill writes most of my boilerplate now
Boilerplate and repetitive code are where it shines

codes.label: Drafts tests, fixtures and mock data
codes.definition: The assistant drafts unit tests, test fixtures or mock data that the developer then adjusts.
codes.include: Any mention of tests, fixtures or mocks being written with it.

anchor_quotes.quote: I describe the case and it drafts the test
It made writing tests less tedious
It writes decent first drafts of test fixtures and mock data

codes.label: Explains unfamiliar code and error messages
codes.definition: The assistant explains code or errors the developer does not understand.
codes.include: Explanations of legacy code, unfamiliar code or error messages.
codes.exclude: Learning a whole new language goes to A-RQ1-04.

anchor_quotes.quote: I ask it to explain unfamiliar code
Explaining legacy code is the best part
It is good at explaining error messages

codes.label: Speeds up learning a new language or framework
codes.definition: The developer learns a new language or framework faster with the assistant.
codes.include: Explicit mention of learning or picking up a technology.
codes.exclude: Explaining a specific piece of code goes to A-RQ1-03.

anchor_quotes.quote: Great for learning a new framework
It helped me pick up Rust much faster than reading the book alone

codes.label: Frees time and attention for higher-level work
codes.definition: Routine work shrinks, so the developer keeps attention for design or stays in context.
codes.include: Time or attention reported as freed for other work, or fewer interruptions to look things up.
codes.exclude: The kind of code it writes goes to A-RQ1-01.

anchor_quotes.quote: I finish routine tickets faster, so I have more time for design work
fewer context switches: I don't have to search the web for syntax
I spend less time on getters, setters and config files

codes.label: Turns notes into documentation
codes.definition: The assistant writes documentation comments from the developer's notes.

anchor_quotes.quote: It turns my notes into readable docstrings

codes.label: Gains limited to routine work
codes.definition: Benefits are reported for routine code only, with a boundary at business logic.
codes.include: Answers that place the benefit on routine work and draw a line where it stops.
codes.exclude: Answers that only praise boilerplate, without a boundary, go to A-RQ1-01.

anchor_quotes.quote: Anything with business logic needs heavy editing
It is fast at boilerplate, but
